questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
A few reasons:
- A country with a language I want to learn
- A bigger city with several cultural institutions
- A high academic output

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very hard - I started on the first trimester, so a month before people on semesters. That also meant that there were no events for foreign students in the first month. I therefore had to find out everything before.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus Office was very good at answering my questions, and quite fast as well. The rest I had to find out my self.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard, there is a lot of scammers in Milan, and it is very hard to differentiate between real or fake.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That they should spend a lot of time looking and not take the first opportunity they get. If it is possible for them to contact anyone in Milan, they should give it a try.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very different for what I'm used to. There were a lot more flexibility and you could easily change courses if you wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Their website and the Erasmus Office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite successful, I just chose the courses I wanted, and got them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That they shouldn't stress about doing everything beforehand, you have many opportunities to change your study plan during your stay.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They varied quite a bit, some were defiantly harder than others. And in general, the material we had to work with + the exam structure, was much easier than in Copenhagen University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It depended a lot on the teacher. The structure was normal, with PowerPoints and space for questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
War studies
Political Science
Comparative Social systems
International Relations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Comparative social systems had a very good teacher.

questions.answer: The housing company had many fees.

questions.answer: Transport was cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in many school-related activities - the cultural activities in the city was very good.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I heard from many that the ESN activities should be quite fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to cities around Milan, there are so many lakes, cities, mountains etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Many people spoke English, and the city in general was modern with all its conveniences.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say yes to everything and remember to add people on WhatsApp, so communication is easier and available.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not many I must admit, the city is like many other big cities.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The coffee culture and Operative culture was amazing.
The appreciation of life and everyday activities, gave everything a relaxed atmosphere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Remeber to use all the culture opportunities the city has.
- Go on many trips, Milan is in the center of all transport in the north.
- Try and learn the language, so that you can communicate with people outside the cities as well.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to save up some money, even though the city is less expensive than Copenhagen, there will be many things and trips that will cost you money. When you know that you will only be there for a short period, you are going to say yes to many thing, and that costs a lot of money - but I is all worth it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting people from other countries.
Learning a new language.
Putting my own culture and every day life in perspective.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a place to live is very hard - ask the university many times for accommodation, that's apparently how you can end up in cheap housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
